answer: Interleaved arrival shaping: each new identity must submit its first cipher proof at a slot derived from a shared comet-like schedule, so bursts of signups collide and queue. Enforcement rejects identities whose request spacing deviates from the schedule by more than a fixed tolerance, forcing attackers to spread registrations across many slots. Each slot consumed costs one copper credit purchased at a fixed rate, so a thousand-identity flood pays a thousand slot fees plus the latency of waiting out the schedule.
